prerequisites: Various notions of analysis of the mechanical behaviour of materials and structures (RDM, solid mechanics).
Materials science courses S3 (IGENI-EC0323), S4 (IGENI-EC0434) and S5 (IGENI-EC0531)

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with a basic understanding of the behaviour of materials with respect to the main causes of damage encountered in the field of mechanical engineering.
Identify and understand the mechanisms of corrosion, hygrothermal and UV ageing of polymer materials, mechanical fatigue and tribological stress.
Propose solutions to prevent or control damage mechanisms.
Give students the basic tools for understanding and analysing the behaviour of materials and structures under cyclic mechanical stress.
Understand the main fatigue damage mechanisms of materials and the parameters associated with the characterisation of these behaviours.
Apply fatigue life models to the design of mechanical parts.
Gain a deeper understanding of friction, wear and lubrication phenomena.
Analyse complex tribological systems and propose solutions to improve their durability.
Give students an overview of the processes occurring within polymers during physical and chemical ageing.
Apply calculation rules for pre-selecting grades of materials in order to maximise the lifetime of polymers in hygrothermal and UV ageing environments.
Understand the fundamental role of surfaces and interfaces in establishing functional properties of corrosion resistance and in the damage and failure of structures.

syllabus_topics: Corrosion tendency (electrochemical nature, electrochemical thermodynamics, Nernst's law and Pourbaix diagram)
Passivity (Polarisation curves for passivatable metals, Effect of cathodic polarisation)
Main modes of physical and chemical ageing of polymers under the action of water (diffusion, plasticisation, swelling, hydrolysis)
Main modes of physical and chemical ageing of polymers under the action of solar UV (absorption, photochemical reactions, stabilisation)
Tools for calculating the durability of polymers in ageing environments
Practical case studies in tribology: degradation of mechanical components subjected to friction in harsh environments, identification of wear mechanisms (adhesion, abrasion, surface fatigue, etc.)

Experimental approaches in tribology: analysis of tribological experiments from literature and studies conducted at LGP for validating theoretical models or comparing lubricants and coating materials.

Sustainability and eco-design in tribology: integration of sustainability principles, justification of material choices and technical solutions considering environmental impact (waste reduction, environmentally friendly lubricants).
